_comment: The rule-carrier registry: a registered rule's other spellings may appear only in its carrier or beside a citation of it. `scope` and `exclude` are path prefixes, not globs, and `exclude` wins.

rules.summary: What CI runs is the set the workspace manifest YIELDS — its own declared recipes plus those its composed packs contribute, namespaced by pack — and not the list it declares. Landed at milestone 7 session 5; cli/recipe-set.mjs is the one carrier of the set and CI calls it rather than enumerating a manifest.
tells: from the manifest and runs each one

rules.summary: The A/B clause's subject is the mandates core SHIPS that an arm actually receives — the kernel's, plus the artifact mandates reachable in a built arm — of which the judgement-only rows are a part. Widened 2026-08-28 on the maintainer's ruling, from a narrower reading that named the judgement rows alone. The narrower reading could not survive measurement: `vendor --host` carries `core/skills/` not at all, so all five judgement rows reach nothing in a vendored arm.
tells: Only the judgement rows are the A/B clause's subject
judgement-only rows are the A/B clause's subject
the A/B clause's subject, not this one's
what the A/B clause exists to reach

rules.summary: The A/B baseline's AGGREGATE figures — the per-arm sum of compliant cells, `6/20` each at the 2026-08-31 capture. Their one carrier is the rendered register. Reduced 2026-09-01: three live sentences (two in `evals/README.md`, one in `evals/ab/arm.md`) restated a sum typed from a reading of the register's rows, with nothing checking them, so a re-run would have left all three stale and silent — this repository's most-named defect class, a hand-maintained figure whose subject can move. The reduction had a precondition the other two rules did not: THE CARRIER DID NOT CARRY THE FIGURE. `baseline.md` rendered per-cell counts only (`5`/5, `0`/5, `0`/5, `1`/5) and the aggregate existed nowhere but in prose, so pointing the sentences at it would have sent a reader to sum four rows by hand. So `cli/ab-run.mjs`'s `renderRegister()` now DERIVES the aggregate from the same cells the rows come from, and it is held by the byte-compare that already held every other line of that document.
rules.incident: Reported by the milestone-8 session-7 handoff `.portulan/handoffs/2026-09-01-a-release-carries-an-eval-result.md`, which found the defect under the `release-eval` clause and deliberately did NOT repair it there because it belongs to the A/B clause. THAT PATH DOES NOT RESOLVE IN THIS TREE, and the citation says so rather than pointing at a file a reader cannot open: it lives on the UNMERGED branch `m8-s7-a-release-carries-an-eval-result`, commit f9009d60, which is not an ancestor of main (main was e192f6b5 when this rule was registered). Verified with `git log --all --diff-filter=A` rather than assumed from the brief, which cited the path as though it were present. NO ISSUE NUMBER IS CITED: `gh` could not be reached from this worktree, and an invented number is worse than a named absence — the other two rules here cite URLs, this one cites the record that exists and where it actually is.
rules._coverage_comment: Blind to the aggregate restated in a file that cites baseline.md, as evals/README.md and evals/ab/arm.md do.
